summary: Across the week, severe geopolitical disruptions around major maritime chokepoints—compounded by escalating US regulatory scrutiny on Chinese commercial vessels—are inflating bunker fuel surcharges and destabilizing global ocean transit times. To mitigate these external vulnerabilities, both India and China are aggressively bolstering domestic supply chain resilience through rail corridor expansions, freight electrification, green port initiatives, and logistics automation. This dual dynamic suggests that persistent ocean freight volatility and compliance risks will accelerate a broader shift toward localized hinterland infrastructure and strategic regional trade alignment.
